data.title: Calendar Invite Injection Phishing — Mass External Calendar Event Creation from New Domains
data.description: Detects calendar injection phishing by identifying mass calendar invite creation from external sources targeting internal users, where the event body contains URLs and the organizer domain is recently registered (under 30 days) or on a high-abuse TLD. Attackers send emails containing .ics calendar attachments or Google Calendar invite links that auto-populate on victim calendars, bypassing email gateway filtering that focuses on message body and attachment analysis. An observed March 2026 campaign delivered 6,000+ emails across 10 sender domains (9 RDGA-generated on .cyou/.sbs/.click TLDs) with antivirus renewal and meeting invite lures. Calendar events persist after email deletion and re-surface via reminder notifications, creating a delayed-action social engineering vector. Recently created organizer accounts (under 7 days) sending calendar invites to 5+ internal recipients are additionally flagged as high-confidence indicators.

detection.condition: selection_external_invite AND filter_new_domain AND filter_urls_in_body AND filter_mass_targeting

enrichment_required.source: Domain age lookup from WHOIS/domain intelligence feed
Top-level domain extracted from organizer email domain
Boolean flag indicating presence of http/https URLs in calendar event description
Days since organizer Google/Microsoft account was created (if available from admin logs)

queries.cql:
// CrowdStrike CQL for Calendar Invite Injection Phishing Detection
// Detects mass external calendar invites from new domains with URLs in event body
(event_type="calendar_invite_received" OR event_type="ics_attachment_processed")
organizer_is_external=true
organizer_domain_age_days<=30
event_body_contains_url=true
| groupBy(organizer_domain, span=24h, function=[
    count(distinct=recipient_email, as=distinct_recipients),
    count(event_id, as=invite_count),
    collect([organizer_email, event_title, organizer_domain_age_days])
  ])
| distinct_recipients >= 5
| sort(distinct_recipients, order=desc)
queries.splunk:
`comment("Splunk SPL for Calendar Invite Injection Phishing Detection")`
`comment("Detects mass external calendar invites from recently-registered domains")`
index=flame_m365 sourcetype=flame:exchange
  (event_type="calendar_invite_received" OR event_type="ics_attachment_processed")
  organizer_is_external="true"
| lookup domain_age_feed organizer_domain OUTPUT domain_age_days, domain_tld
| where domain_age_days < 30
| where match(event_body, "https?://")
| bin _time span=24h
| stats dc(recipient_email) AS distinct_recipients, count AS invite_count,
    values(organizer_email) AS organizers, values(event_title) AS event_titles,
    values(domain_age_days) AS domain_age, values(domain_tld) AS tlds
    by organizer_domain, _time
| where distinct_recipients >= 5
| eval risk_level = case(
    domain_age_days < 7 AND distinct_recipients > 50, "critical",
    domain_age_days < 7 OR distinct_recipients > 20, "high",
    1=1, "medium")
| eval high_abuse_tld = if(match(domain_tld, "cyou|sbs|click|top|xyz|biz"), "true", "false")
| sort - distinct_recipients
queries.sql:
-- SQL for Calendar Invite Injection Phishing Detection
-- Detects mass external calendar invites from newly-registered domains with URLs
SELECT
  ce.organizer_domain,
  d.domain_age_days,
  d.tld AS domain_tld,
  COUNT(DISTINCT ce.recipient_email) AS distinct_recipients,
  COUNT(*) AS invite_count,
  STRING_AGG(DISTINCT ce.organizer_email, ', ') AS organizer_emails,
  STRING_AGG(DISTINCT ce.event_title, ', ') AS event_titles,
  MIN(ce.event_created_timestamp) AS first_invite,
  MAX(ce.event_created_timestamp) AS last_invite,
  CASE
    WHEN d.domain_age_days < 7 AND COUNT(DISTINCT ce.recipient_email) > 50 THEN 'critical'
    WHEN d.domain_age_days < 7 OR COUNT(DISTINCT ce.recipient_email) > 20 THEN 'high'
    ELSE 'medium'
  END AS risk_level,
  CASE
    WHEN d.tld IN ('.cyou', '.sbs', '.click', '.top', '.xyz', '.biz') THEN TRUE
    ELSE FALSE
  END AS high_abuse_tld
FROM calendar_events ce
JOIN domain_intelligence d ON ce.organizer_domain = d.domain_name
WHERE ce.organizer_is_external = TRUE
  AND ce.event_created_timestamp >= DATEADD(HOUR, -24, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)
  AND d.domain_age_days <= 30
  AND ce.event_body LIKE '%http%'
GROUP BY ce.organizer_domain, d.domain_age_days, d.tld
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ce.recipient_email) >= 5
ORDER BY distinct_recipients DESC

references: Malwarebytes Labs, Calendar Phishing Campaign Analysis (February 2026)
Google Workspace Security, Advisory on External Calendar Invite Auto-Accept Settings
Infoblox, RDGA Domain Analysis and Zone File Monitoring Methodology
FBI IC3, Tech Support Scam PSAs — downstream calendar phishing impact
falsepositives: Legitimate external event organizers (conference providers, webinar platforms) using newly registered event-specific domains
Marketing partners sending calendar invites for scheduled meetings or product demos
Automated meeting scheduling tools (Calendly, HubSpot) from new customer domains
